 Shraddha Kapoor Brings The Adaa, Drama And Fire As Eetha In ‘Ji Ji Re Ji’
 MISS MALINI | 17.NOV.2026 Link copied to clipboard 
 Shraddha Kapoor is bringing a whole new energy to the screen with her latest avatar as Eetha. After giving us a glimpse of the legendary artist in the film’s trailer, the actress now steps into the spotlight with ‘Ji Ji Re Ji’ , the first song from Eetha .
 And if the trailer had us curious about this world, the song gives us a much better look at it.
 Presented by Maddock Films and Kathputli Creations, ‘Ji Ji Re Ji’ is steeped in the colour, rhythm and drama of Lavani, with Shraddha dressed in a traditional Nauvari sari, jewellery and ghungroo as she takes centre stage as Eetha.
 But there’s more to the song than its vibrant visuals.
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by Shraddha ✶ (@shraddhakapoor) 
 It introduces us to Eetha as an artist who knows exactly how to command attention. The expressions, the adaayein and the confidence with which Shraddha moves across the stage make it clear that Eetha’s story is as much about her presence as it is about her journey.
 The song brings together quite the musical team, with Ajay-Atul composing the music, Amitabh Bhattacharya on lyrics and Shreya Ghoshal lending her vocals. The result is an energetic Lavani track that feels rooted in tradition while carrying the larger-than-life scale of a cinematic performance.
 And then there’s Vaibhavi Merchant’s choreography , which gives Shraddha plenty of room to bring Eetha to life.
 Speaking about the song, Shraddha says stepping into Lavani was both exhilarating and nerve-wracking, especially because the song marks a significant moment in Eetha’s story. And judging by the performance, she has clearly embraced every bit of the challenge.
 Also Read: Shraddha Kapoor’s EETHA Trailer To Play Alongside Ramayana In Cinemas This Diwali 
 For Ajay-Atul, the idea was to make the music feel like an extension of Eetha herself, capturing her strength, charisma and spirit rather than simply functioning as a soundtrack.
 Shreya Ghoshal also describes ‘Ji Ji Re Ji’ as one of those songs she got to “live” for a few minutes, and her voice brings exactly the kind of energy the performance demands.
 What makes the song interesting is how it gives us a glimpse beyond the performer. Behind all the stage lights, dance and adaayein is a woman with her own struggles, ambition and story, and Eetha seems ready to explore all of it.
 With Shraddha stepping fully into the character and ‘Ji Ji Re Ji’ setting the stage, we’re definitely curious to see what Eetha’s story has in store.
 ‘Ji Ji Re Ji’ is out now. 
 Eetha , directed by Laxman Utekar and produced by Dinesh Vijan, Laxman Utekar, and Karishma Sharma, releases in cinemas on December 4, 2026 .
